newsitem.title: USA: "Space Jam" shoots to top of U.S. box office.
newsitem.headline: "Space Jam" shoots to top of U.S. box office.

text.p: "Space Jam," a comedy starring basketball player Michael Jordan and a host of cartoon characters led by Bugs Bunny, shot to the top of the U.S. box office in its opening weekend, according to studio estimates released Sunday.
The film earned $29.25 million in the Friday to Sunday period, comfortably ahead of last week's number one, "Ransom," which slipped to second with $23.0 million.
Barbra Streisand's latest movie, "The Mirror Has Two Faces," opened in third with $12.2 million, the actress' best opening tally.

"Space Jam" mixes live action and animation as Jordan coaches a team of Looney Tunes characters in a basketball match against alien invaders. It is released by Warner Bros., a unit of Time Warner Inc..

"Ransom," a Walt Disney Co. thriller in which Mel Gibson plays an airline mogul who turns the tables on his son's kidnappers, fell 33 percent from its opening weekend score of $34.2 million. Its 10-day gross is $68 million.

Some distance behind in third was "The Mirror Has Two Faces," which Streisand also directed and produced. The romantic comedy/drama is released by Sony Corp.'s Columbia Pictures. Her last movie, 1991's "The Prince Of Tides," opened with $10 million and went on to make $75 million, a Sony spokesman said.

Slipping one place to fourth was the female bank robber drama, "Set It Off," with $5.8 million. The film, which is released by Time Warner's New Line Cinema, has grossed $7.5 million after 12 days of release.

In fifth with $5.6 million was the MTV-styled "William Shakespeare's Romeo & Juliet." Down from second last weekend, the movie has made $31.6 million after 17 days. It is released by News Corp.'s 20th Century Fox.
